messages.message: Analyze the optical and SAR images together.
This analysis compares a standard optical satellite photo with a radar (SAR) satellite capture. Combining both gives a much clearer understanding of land features, moisture, and man-made structures.

answer.summary: This analysis compares a standard optical satellite photo with a radar (SAR) satellite capture. Combining both gives a much clearer understanding of land features, moisture, and man-made structures.
key_findings: Buildings & Hard Surfaces: Reflect radar strongly and appear very bright in the radar view (covers about 52.7% of the scene).
Water & Flat Surfaces: Absorb or deflect radar waves and appear dark (covers about 9.4% of the area).
Trees & Forest Foliage: Scatter the radar signals in all directions with medium texture (covers about 37.9%).
Cloud Penetration: Radar passes right through clouds and haze, capturing the ground even in poor weather.
answer.explanation: What this means: Standard satellite cameras take photos using sunlight, but can be blocked by weather and clouds. Radar satellites send down radio waves that pierce through clouds to measure surface texture, moisture, and buildings. In the side-by-side comparison below, you can see how optical colors compare directly with radar reflections.

technical_details.preprocessing_info: Log-decibel calibrated SAR amplitude combined with 2%-98% contrast stretched optical reflectance.
